speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo. To help narrow this down, have these episodes been accompanied by severe headaches, sensitivity to light or sound, or visual disturbances like flashing lights?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the dizziness is position-dependent in a 70-year-old woman, could you tell me if these episodes are triggered specifically by lying down, rolling over in bed, or looking up? Also, have you noticed any ringing in your ears or hearing loss on one side during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical picture of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old with presbycusis and no auditory symptoms is classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal.
